problem: The answer says P(X≤45) "includes the whole block at 45", then says using 45.5 "includes half the block that would otherwise be missed". Read together the two sentences look contradictory, and a student may think the correction adds only half of the mass at 45 rather than the whole block (44.5 to 45.5).
fix: A binomial count takes whole numbers, so all the probability at 45 sits in one block from 44.5 to 45.5. The normal curve is continuous, so we must give it an interval. Using 45 as the limit would cut the block at 45 in half and lose the part from 45 to 45.5. Using the upper edge 45.5 includes the whole block at 45, so P(X≤45) is estimated by P(Y≤45.5) for the normal variable Y.
